cases.customer_question: Can I avoid IOPT testing when reusing a reference design if I do not modify profiles or ICS items?
question_variants: Is IOPT testing required if I reuse profiles without changes?
Can I skip IOPT if I don't change ICS items?
When does IOPT apply under QPRD v4?
Do unchanged profiles still require IOPT testing?
How to avoid IOPT testing in qualification?
cases.actual_issue: Understanding updated IOPT applicability under QPRD v4 when reusing profiles without modifying ICS items.
cases.plain_english_explanation: IOPT testing checks interoperability for certain higher-layer features. Under newer rules, not all reused features automatically require IOPT anymore. If you reuse features exactly as-is without changing them, you may not need to run those tests.
cases.consultant_answer: Under QPRD v4, the rule for IOPT generation changed. Previously, inheriting profiles from a referenced design triggered IOPT automatically. Now, IOPT is only required for profiles where ICS items have been added, removed, or modified after referencing. If a profile is reused without any ICS changes or is removed entirely from the design, IOPT is not generated for that profile.
cases.decision_logic: IOPT requirement is triggered by ICS modifications to X2Core layers after referencing a design; no ICS change → no IOPT.
cases.final_recommendation: Ensure that reused profiles are either unchanged or removed entirely. Avoid modifying ICS items to eliminate IOPT test requirements.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: If ICS changes are made unintentionally, IOPT tests will be required, leading to additional testing cost, time, and potential delays.
